items.title: Comcast’s Dividend Keeps Growing While the Market Treats It Like a Melting Ice Cube
items.summary: Comcast sits near a 52-week low with a fresh Sell rating, yet its free cash flow dwarfs what it costs to pay shareholders every quarter. Something in that math deserves a closer look before the market's verdict gets accepted as fact.

items.title: Want Income Now? 3 Stocks Paying 5% or More and the Risk That Comes With Each
items.summary: Three stocks all yield above 5% and all carry decades of unbroken dividend payments, but each one asks you to accept a completely different kind of risk before that income hits your account.

items.title: ‘They Get You Coming In, They Get You Going Out’: Clark’s Fix for T-Mobile’s Exit Bill Trap
items.summary: T-Mobile billed Luke in Virginia for an extra month after he cancelled, and the supervisor refused to budge. Clark Howard says carriers have engineered this trap into every billing cycle, but a simple date on your calendar closes it.

items.title: 3 U.S. Dividend Stocks Offering Defensive Income as Fed Rate Pressure Persists
items.summary: With traders bracing for another possible 0.25% Fed hike in October, solid labor data and firm inflation keep pressure on anything seen as risky. Defensive dividend stocks suddenly feel less boring and more like a potential anchor for a jumpier market, especially for investors who care about steady income when policy stays tight. items.title: Can Verizon Communications (VZ) Stay Cheap As 6G Plans Expand?
items.summary: Verizon Communications has delivered a strong 3 year share price gain, yet recent weekly and monthly declines mean investors are again asking whether the current valuation lines up with its earnings power. With the business stepping up activity around next generation networks and AI related initiatives, the key issue is how much profit the market is assuming those plans can eventually support. items.title: The Cheapest Stocks in the S&P 500: Are They a Bargain or a Trap?
items.summary: Inflation is stubbornly high, but not in home broadband service.  There, telecom operators are making fiberoptic inroads in a business long dominated by cable television companies.  The result has been discounting:  UBS  reports that prices for various broadband service tiers are down 7% to 14% for fiber over the past year, and 17% to 27% for cable.
